Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data scientist with experience building and evaluating forecasting, churn and experimentation solutions using Python, SQL and cloud-based data tools. Developed scheduled and batch-scored machine learning workflows, engineered model features, and introduced pytest coverage for forecasting feature code. MSc in Statistics with a dissertation on Bayesian hierarchical models; now seeking to develop further in machine learning engineering.

CORE SKILLS
Programming and analysis: Python, SQL, R
Machine learning: LightGBM, XGBoost, scikit-learn, pandas, SHAP, feature engineering, forecasting, churn modelling
Data and cloud tools: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, Looker
Engineering and applications: pytest, Docker, Streamlit, scheduled notebooks, batch scoring
Statistics and experimentation: Bayesian hierarchical models, experimental design, sequential A/B testing, statsmodels
Additional learning: PyTorch, torchvision (course project)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox | 2022-Present
- Built a six-week-ahead weekly recipe-demand forecasting workflow using LightGBM and calendar, price and menu-position features. The scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook writes forecasts to BigQuery for operational use in Looker.
- Improved forecast WAPE from 23% to 14%; the project estimated a 9% reduction in food waste.
- Developed a weekly XGBoost churn-scoring workflow in BigQuery and used top-decile scores to target retention offers. A 10% holdout validation showed churn was 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated group.
- Built a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests, used by approximately 25 people in product and growth. Wrote the app and Dockerfile; the data platform team handles deployment to Cloud Run.
- Began writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025; coverage is approximately 60%.
- Delivered the internal training session “Stats for PMs” three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | 2020-2022
- Segmented customers and analysed tariffs using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days each month.

ADDITIONAL PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | 2025
- Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset as part of an online deep learning course; achieved approximately 80% accuracy.
- Tools: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.

EDUCATION
MSc in Statistics
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models
docs.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role at Quillstone Payments. In my current data science work, I build forecasting, churn-scoring and experimentation solutions that connect model outputs to operational decisions, and I am keen to develop that experience further on a team taking AI ideas from prototype to production.

At Thistlebox, I built a scheduled LightGBM forecasting workflow that writes six-week-ahead recipe and region forecasts to BigQuery for operational use in Looker. WAPE improved from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I also developed a weekly XGBoost churn-scoring workflow in BigQuery; a 10% holdout validation showed churn was 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated group. These projects have given me practical experience in feature engineering, evaluation and data workflows supporting business operations.

I have also built a Streamlit application for sequential A/B testing, used by around 25 colleagues in product and growth. I wrote its Dockerfile, while the data platform team manages deployment to Cloud Run. Since 2025, I have added pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage. My MSc in Statistics, including a dissertation on Bayesian hierarchical models, supports this applied work with a grounding in modelling uncertainty and experimental design.

Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants and its Customer Operations AI team’s work on answering questions and routing tickets make this role particularly interesting to me. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my applied modelling and collaboration experience while developing further in the engineering practices needed to operate machine learning systems in production. Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
